introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0760), Paper 2 - Cameroon History Since 1800, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections. All the questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Regle de choix : le sujet impose « answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections » (3 sections : A 1800-1922, B 1922-1961, C 1961 to present, 4 questions chacune, numerotation continue 1 a 12). `regles_choix` porte le minimum impose, une regle `parmi 1 sur 4` par section ; la regle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable et est recopiee dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : chaque question est imprimee « (25 marks) » et la page de garde dit « All the questions carry equal marks » ; `points` de l'exercice et de la question unique valent 25. Aucun ecart avec le sujet (4 x 25 = 100).

Defauts d'impression du sujet : scan de deux pages (CamScanner) avec filigrane gcerevision.com et bandeau publicitaire, sans incidence sur la lecture, mais avec une legere transparence de texte (verso) en haut de la page 2 et entre quelques questions ; les intitules de section sont imprimes avec un tiret demi-cadratin (« 1800 - 1922 ») recopie avec un tiret simple ; la question 2 est imprimee « succeed to extend » (tournure incorrecte, recopiee telle quelle) ; la question 3 est ambigue (« the results of German annexation by 1884 ») ; la question 6 est maladroite (« indigenous resistance and failure against French rule »). Aucune figure, carte ni document dans le sujet. Page de garde verifiee : ADVANCED LEVEL, History 2, Paper 2 - Cameroon History Since 1800, code 0760, JUNE 2026 (reference GCE26/0760/2/BN).

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees de memoire, sans acces a une source. Les dates, noms et traites sont ceux de l'historiographie etablie ; les faits dont la precision est moindre sont formules prudemment ou sans chiffre. Aucune citation, statistique ni source n'est inventee. Les corriges sont a relire par un historien du Cameroun avant diffusion.

Question 12 : question la plus delicate du sujet, car de nombreux faits sont contestes et mal documentes (versions officielles contre versions des partisans d'Ahidjo). Dates retenues avec prudence : demission d'Ahidjo le 4 novembre 1982 et prestation de serment de Biya le 6 novembre 1982 ; demission d'Ahidjo de la presidence de l'UNC et remplacement du Premier ministre Bello Bouba Maigari par Luc Ayang en aout 1983 ; accusation de complot contre Ahidjo en aout 1983 ; proces par contumace et condamnation a mort en fevrier 1984 (commuee) ; tentative de coup d'Etat du 6 avril 1984 de la Garde republicaine ; changement de nom en « Republique du Cameroun » en janvier-fevrier 1984 ; creation du RDPC en mars 1985 (congres de Bamenda) ; mort d'Ahidjo a Dakar en novembre 1989. Aucun bilan chiffre des victimes de 1984 n'est donne (les estimations varient). A faire relire par un historien du Cameroun avant diffusion.

questions.enonce_markdown:
For what reasons and with what impact did a rift erupt between Ahidjo and Biya shortly after 1982?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** On 4 November 1982 President Ahmadou Ahidjo, who had ruled Cameroon since independence, announced his resignation, officially for health reasons, and handed over to his Prime Minister, Paul Biya, who took the oath on 6 November. Ahidjo, a Muslim Northerner, expected to keep influence by remaining the head of the single party, the Cameroon National Union (CNU). Within months a serious rift opened between the two men, which ended in exile for Ahidjo, a trial in absentia and a coup attempt in 1984. The facts are partly disputed, so this answer gives the generally accepted account.

**1. Reasons for the rift.**
(a) *The question of power.* Ahidjo kept the presidency of the CNU, which in a single-party state was the real centre of power, and he seems to have thought that Biya, a Southerner of the Beti-Bulu group and a civil servant without a strong political base, would remain under his control. Biya, once president, wanted to exercise the full powers of his office. The dual leadership, one man in the Presidency and one at the head of the party, was bound to cause conflict.
(b) *Biya's political style and policies.* Biya promised a "New Deal" (*Renouveau national*) with "rigour and moralisation", which implied criticism of the management and the corruption of the previous regime and a break with Ahidjo's methods.
(c) *Changes in the government and security services.* Biya replaced some of Ahidjo's appointees and loyalists and promoted his own supporters in the government and army, notably by changing the Prime Minister (the Northerner Bello Bouba Maigari, appointed in 1982, was replaced in August 1983 by Luc Ayang) and others; Ahidjo regarded this as interference with the arrangements he had made.
(d) *Ahidjo's criticism and interference.* From his residence in France and from Cameroon, Ahidjo criticised Biya's decisions, tried to influence appointments through the party and reportedly kept contacts with supporters in the administration and army, which Biya saw as a threat.
(e) *Regional and ethnic rivalries.* There was tension between the Northerners, who had held key positions under Ahidjo, and the Southerners who gained influence under Biya. The Northern elite feared losing its power and its place in the army and the administration.
(f) *Suspicion and plot allegations.* In August 1983 Biya's government announced that it had discovered a plot to remove him and accused Ahidjo and his followers of planning a coup, which the Ahidjoists denied. Ahidjo resigned as president of the CNU in August 1983.

**2. Impact.**
(a) *Fall and exile of Ahidjo.* Ahidjo went into exile, first in France and then in Senegal, and in February 1984 was tried in absentia by a military court and sentenced to death (Biya commuted the sentence). He died in Dakar in November 1989.
(b) *Purge of Ahidjo's supporters.* Ministers, officers and officials seen as loyal to Ahidjo were removed, arrested, tried or marginalised.
(c) *The 1984 coup attempt.* On 6 April 1984 part of the Republican Guard, composed largely of Northern soldiers, tried to overthrow Biya and fought in Yaoundé; the coup was defeated, followed by arrests and executions of many suspected participants, and its effect was to strengthen Biya's power and to increase north-south mistrust.
(d) *Consolidation of Biya's power.* He took control of the party, which was renamed the Cameroon People's Democratic Movement (CPDM) in 1985, abolished the post of Prime Minister (1984; it was restored in 1991), renamed the state "Republic of Cameroon" (1984) and reorganised the army and the administration so that power was concentrated in the President.
(e) *Regional and ethnic effects.* The rift increased the distrust between North and South, and the sense that the Northern elite had lost power; the army was reorganised and more Southern officers were promoted.
(f) *Political effects.* It brought a more repressive phase at the start of Biya's rule, with arrests of opponents, and it delayed the political liberalisation that came only after 1990 under the pressure of the economic crisis and of the opposition.
(g) *External relations.* France, which had good relations with both men, kept its support for the Biya government, and Nigeria and other neighbours watched closely.

**Conclusion.** The rift between Ahidjo and Biya in 1982-1984 arose from the contest for real power between a president and the party chief who had handed over to him, from differences of style and policy, from the dismissal of Ahidjo's men and from regional rivalries. Its impact was the exile and condemnation of Ahidjo, the purge of his supporters, the failed coup of April 1984 and the consolidation of Biya's personal power, with lasting north-south tensions.
